Lists Kawangi (UR-68, pop. 50, p. 542) and Weleki (UR-69, pop. 130, p. 543) as separate Uruwa Family entries: 'The people are being assimilated by the Timbe and Selepet peoples, and, as is the case with Kawangi, further field work is necessary.' sources.note: Nothing. Weliki appears only in sec. 2.5.5 (p. 56): 'Another language which may be within the Uruwa Family is spoken at the villages of Karangi and Weleki in the lower Timbe and Selepet areas.. word lists collected from the two villages show considerable borrowing from these languages.' No wordlist printed, no phonology. (The 'stressed syllable' passage on pp. 4-5 of the same volume is Bunn & Bunn's Golin phonology, unrelated.)
